sentence: This project builds a heart simulator for each patient that lets surgeons compare repair techniques for children with single-ventricle physiology.
This project studies how a protein that is mutated in ovarian cancer changes epigenetic control of repetitive elements so immune cells attack tumors.
This project studies the molecular mechanisms that control neuroinflammation in the central nervous system and how they relate to Alzheimer's Disease.
This project uses genetic screens to find genes that help cells from hibernating Arctic ground squirrel and nematodes survive hypothermia and hypoxia.
This project provides standardized immunologic assays to study how chronic HIV infection affects people, including aging and frailty.
This project studies how modifications of viral RNA affect viral translation and how the host cell innate immune system senses viral RNAs.
This project tries to find out which molecular mechanisms control the development and connectivity of respiratory neurons, to help with breathing disorders.
This project builds a computational system that uses cell-free DNA to detect adverse outcomes of cancer treatment, such as recurrence and side effects.
This project studies how brain cells use energy from glucose and how this changes with brain activity and among cell types.
This project tries to find out how cells sense and resolve ionic stress caused by elevated intracellular ionic strength.
This project uses computational analysis to study how osteoporosis therapies affect osteoblast progenitors and osteocytes in post-menopausal women and female mice.
This project studies how biological processes at the molecular scale give rise to functions at the levels of the whole body.
This project studies how macrophages and fibroblasts communicate, how macrophages decide to migrate, and how fibroblasts change the extracellular matrix.
This project tests whether bacterial enzymes called DNA methyltransferases help drive colon cancer by promoting bacterial virulence and modifying the human cell genome.
This project builds a computer-aided diagnostic tool that gives intuitive explanations for its results, aiming at better diagnostic accuracy and clinician trust.
This project studies how cancer-associated genes work and uses genome sequencing to help match cancer treatments to each tumor.
This project studies how different dopaminergic neurons and their circuits support learning and memory.
This project builds a secure data management system and provides statistical and bioinformatics support for a malaria research center.
This project studies how oxidative damage to guanine in DNA, and its repair, affects the regulation of gene expression in human cells.
This project studies how exosomes and their RNA cargo work in heart failure and tests whether they can serve as markers and targets for therapy.
